escalations: Census structure: two of my movements end at a boundary with no successor entry for the same church. (1) The late Anglo-Saxon legacy says the dioceses 'carried straight on into the Norman and later medieval English church', but no census entry covers the English church from 1066 to the Reformation, so that continuity has nowhere to go. (2) The Scandinavian legacy says the conversion-era dioceses were 'reformed rather than replaced at the Reformation', but no entry covers the Scandinavian church from 1104 to the 1520s; I drafted the continued-as link straight to scandinavian-reformation-kingdoms (era 7) at Inferential-Thin. Whether that four-century span should stand, or wait for medieval entries, is a census-structure call.

Unsourced no-entry claims, left as written for the entry owner: much of the late Anglo-Saxon and Scandinavian text rests on texts not vendored and not cited anywhere in the repo.
